# The step-cap depth formula fails at eight triangle fibers
product-chain depth formula and separately computes the original residual
program for the step-cap cover. It does not assert those step caps remain
globally critical when the depth formula fails.

## 1. An exact oblique cap beats the proposed step depth

Let T be a triangle of area one and g its centroid. For m>=1 consider
S={0,...,2m-1} times T. At the left middle point (m-1,g), normalize a
canonical vertex direction so the projected vertex values are(-1,-1,2).
Its upper tail is F(s)=((2-s)/3)^2 on -1<=s<=2. Set

    L=6/(2m^2+1).

At relative base k=z-(m-1), k=-(m-1),...,m, the single ambient cap
u.(x-g)>=L k has threshold kL. All these thresholds lie in[-1,2]:
6(m-1)<=2m^2+1 and 6m<=2(2m^2+1). The two sums

    sum k=m,
    sum k^2=m(2m^2+1)/3

give its EXACT mass

    sum_k F(kL)
       =[8m-4mL+m(2m^2+1)L^2/3]/9
       =4m(4m^2-1)/[9(2m^2+1)].                         (1)

Its difference from the proposed step depth m-1+4/9 is

    [-2m^3+10m^2-13m+5]/[9(2m^2+1)].                   (2)

For m=4 this is -5/99. More generally the numerator is negative for
all integers m>=4: it equals-15 at4, and its successive difference is
-6m^2+14m-5<0 for m>=4. Thus the proposed value is too large already
at eight fibers and remains too large for every longer even chain.

For completeness this is a GLOBAL upper-bound obstruction, not merely
an assertion that one proposed center fails. Within each fiber the
centroid is depth-maximal: the affine maps permuting the triangle's
vertices preserve T, its uniform measure, the mixed set and the ambient
halfspace family. A depth region within the fiber is convex (it is the
intersection of the complements of all too-small caps). Averaging the
orbit of any point under these permutations gives g, so the centroid
has at least that point's depth. Reflection of the base about m-1/2
preserves the measure; the segment between a fiber centroid and its
reflection contains both middle centroids whenever the original base
is outside the middle pair. Convexity of the full ambient depth regions
therefore makes the middle centroids maximal among all fiber centroids.
These middle points themselves belong to S. Thus(1) is also a global
upper bound. Alternatively, for the eight-fiber
case every nonmiddle fiber has the isolating bound at most2+4/9, below
112/33, and the following refinement controls every point of the middle
fibers directly. Pick a barycentric coordinate exceeding1/3 away from g,
use its canonical direction in the cap of(1), and move its source trace
from g to that point. Every captured contribution decreases and the
source contribution decreases strictly. Reflection handles the other
middle fiber.

At m=4, therefore,

    max raw depth <=112/33 <31/9=3+4/9.                 (3)

The detailed all-normal lower bound establishing equality in(3) is a
separate result. The strict upper bound already disproves the step-depth
formula and proves that the middle step caps of mass31/9 are not globally
critical.

## 2. The step-cover residual program still has an exact general formula

Now let T be a volume-one d-simplex, d>=1, gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, and
c=(1-gamma)^(1/d). Take the step canonical caps based at the two middle
centroids: left caps capture every lower base, their own canonical cap,
and no higher base; right caps are reflected. They form a genuine
ambient cap cover, whether or not they are globally critical. The
original residual obstacles are

    e=(0,...,0,c,c,0,...,0),

with the two c entries at m-1,m. For d>1, strict convexity and reflection
force a symmetric optimizer; convexity makes every height at least its
middle height, which is at least c. Thus h is uniquely constant c.
For d=1 the same constant vector is an optimizer; the formulas below
refer to that valid chosen primal and KKT system. Put s=d c^(d-1), with
s=1 when d=1.

The nearest-neighbor multipliers are

    beta_j/s=j(j+1)/2                 (0<=j<=m-1),
    beta_(2m-1-j)=beta_j,
    lambda_(m-1)=lambda_m=m s,
    lambda_j=0 otherwise.                              (4)

These follow by the exact recurrence
lambda_j=s+2beta_j-beta_(j-1)-beta_(j+1), endpoint beta=0, and the
strict obstacle slack outside the two middle sites. For d>1 they are
the unique nearest-neighbor multipliers. For m=1 both beta values are0
and the two rows stop immediately.

For m>=2 the ORIGINAL terminal row from the left middle source is

    theta_j=(m+1)/(2m^2)    for 0<=j<=m-1,
    theta_j=(m-1)/(2m^2)    for m<=j<=2m-1.             (5)

One verifies this without guessing a new coupling. Set
W_j=(beta_j/s)theta_j on the positive-beta indices. Away from the two
middle indices, the Green equation reduces to the recurrence in(4).
At the middle indices, writing a=m(m-1)/2 and the two constants in(5)
as A,B, the equations are

    (a+m)A-aB=1,
    (a+m)B-aA=0.

Their unique solution is exactly(5). The endpoint absorption weights
are W_1=A and W_(2m-2)=B, as required by the original Green formula.
The row has mass one and barycenter m-1.

For a left step cap, its residual roots are zero at the m-1 lower bases,
c at its source, and one at the m upper bases. Hence the exact row loss is

    sum theta_j f_j-c
       =(m-1)[m-(2m+1)c]/(2m^2)<0                     (6)

for m>=2, because c>=1/2 and m/(2m+1)<1/2. The d=1 case has c=1/2;
for d>=2, gamma<=4/9 makes c>1/2. The right row is symmetric.

The Green boundary terms are also explicit. For m>=2, only the indices
m-2,m-1,m can have nonzero second differences, namely c,1-2c,c-1.
Their coefficients are

    W_(m-2)=(m-2)(m-1)(m+1)/(4m^2),
    W_(m-1)=(m^2-1)/(4m),
    W_m=(m-1)^2/(4m).

The first coefficient is zero at m=2; otherwise it is a positive term
at an empty-residual transit node. Their exact weighted sum is(6).
Thus this whole family has explicit compensation in its ORIGINAL rows,
but after the step caps cease to be critical it cannot be substituted
for a theorem about all globally critical cap menus.
